{
  "world_id": "wld_abyssal_shares",
  "characters": [
    {
      "id": "chr_ilya_voss",
      "name": "Ilya Voss",
      "role": "protagonist",
      "description": "Director of Pelagic Biologics' brood program, Ilya grew up in a family of contract handlers and learned to read animal behavior before she learned to trust corporate reports. She recognized the leviathan's feeding-light patterns as responses rather than reflexes, but filed the first evidence as a husbandry anomaly to protect her program. She is lean, close-cropped, and usually wears a pressure-rated work jacket marked with old enclosure scratches.",
      "motivation": "Preserve the leviathan as a living, communicating being rather than let Meridian reduce it to a harvest.",
      "goal": "Reach the Brood Vault and secure a way to isolate and transport the animal intact before the Pressure Gate decision is made.",
      "flaw": "She treats custody as protection and assumes that the right to understand a creature gives her the right to control it.",
      "internal_conflict": "Her genuine care for the leviathan is entangled with her desire to vindicate the breeding program she helped conceal.",
      "external_conflict": "Meridian plans a lethal harvest, while Keelward's lockdown blocks access to the Brood Vault and the Shared Current makes consent and containment uncertain.",
      "arc": "Ilya begins convinced that Pelagic custody is the only alternative to destruction. When the Shared Current exposes the workers' memories of her concealed anomaly report, she must choose whether to disclose the report and give the linked workers a say, even if that costs her control of the animal. She ends willing to defend the leviathan without claiming ownership of its choices.",
      "personality_traits": [
        "observant",
        "patient",
        "possessive",
        "methodical"
      ],
      "abilities": [
        {
          "name": "Behavioral reading",
          "description": "Interprets changes in the leviathan's feeding-light and current patterns by comparing them with its prior enclosure behavior.",
          "category": "mental"
        },
        {
          "name": "Brood protocol knowledge",
          "description": "Knows the enclosure's routine controls and Pelagic's custody procedures, but cannot override other contractors' systems.",
          "category": "technological"
        }
      ],
      "faction_id": "fac_pelagic_biologics",
      "home_location_id": "loc_brood_vault"
    },
    {
      "id": "chr_marek_sato",
      "name": "Marek Sato",
      "role": "protagonist",
      "description": "Meridian Extraction's department head, Marek built his career on turning uncertain tissue into traceable, export-grade batches. He rose from ledger clerk to plant chief by keeping production moving through shortages, and still carries a sample ledger sealed in a waterproof sleeve. He has a square build, a precise clipped manner, and centrifuge burns along one glove where he once handled a failed batch himself.",
      "motivation": "Keep the colony's workers and systems from collapsing into an uncontrolled crisis.",
      "goal": "Stop the Enzyme Works from failing and prevent an undocumented harvest from being passed off as commercial stock.",
      "flaw": "He reduces human safety to measurable production thresholds and trusts records more readily than people.",
      "internal_conflict": "He knows production incentives helped bind workers' housing and renewals to output, yet he fears that admitting this will make every sacrifice he demanded seem meaningless.",
      "external_conflict": "Pelagic's intact-capture plan threatens the production line, while the Shared Current disrupts ordinary work and the two-signature sample chain prevents him from acting alone.",
      "arc": "Marek begins believing that a controlled harvest is the only rational way to preserve the colony. When the Shared Current lets him experience the same alarm remembered by workers he had treated as production figures, he must choose whether to halt processing and disclose the limits of the sample records. He ends prepared to accept lost output rather than call an untraceable harvest safe.",
      "personality_traits": [
        "exact",
        "pragmatic",
        "defensive",
        "persistent"
      ],
      "abilities": [
        {
          "name": "Batch accounting",
          "description": "Tracks tissue provenance, custody signatures, and production bottlenecks across the Enzyme Works.",
          "category": "mental"
        },
        {
          "name": "Process control",
          "description": "Can operate and diagnose the plant's validated processing line, which is not a substitute for authority over the station or brood.",
          "category": "technological"
        }
      ],
      "faction_id": "fac_meridian_extraction",
      "home_location_id": "loc_enzymeworks"
    },
    {
      "id": "chr_tamsin_reed",
      "name": "Tamsin Reed",
      "role": "protagonist",
      "description": "Keelward Logistics' station-safety chief, Tamsin was trained to maintain pressure boundaries and evacuation routes in habitats where one bad seal can cost an entire crew. She ordered the Pressure Gate sealed after incompatible contamination reports, then kept the reason close while Pelagic and Meridian fought over access. Broad-shouldered and silver-haired, she marks every manual control with a strip of tactile tape for use in poor visibility.",
      "motivation": "Get the trapped workers to safety without turning the Pressure Gate into a route for a recovery team or a hazard.",
      "goal": "Determine whether the gate can be opened for evacuation without exposing the colony to a greater danger.",
      "flaw": "She confuses keeping control with keeping people safe and withholds decisions until she can bear their consequences alone.",
      "internal_conflict": "Her duty to evacuate workers conflicts with her fear that opening the gate will make her responsible for whatever passes through it.",
      "external_conflict": "The gate's floodable service chamber makes either choice costly, and the other contractors can block systems she needs to carry out an evacuation.",
      "arc": "Tamsin begins with the Pressure Gate sealed and treats unilateral control as the safest option. When the Shared Current reveals that workers may coordinate an evacuation but cannot be assumed to agree, she must choose to share the gate decision and its risks with them rather than issue another unexplained order. She ends still cautious, but willing to make safety a negotiated responsibility.",
      "personality_traits": [
        "disciplined",
        "protective",
        "reserved",
        "stubborn"
      ],
      "abilities": [
        {
          "name": "Pressure-system diagnosis",
          "description": "Recognizes pressure hazards and can judge the operational risks of the gate's manual controls.",
          "category": "technological"
        },
        {
          "name": "Emergency coordination",
          "description": "Organizes crews around evacuation procedures when communications and access remain available.",
          "category": "social"
        }
      ],
      "faction_id": "fac_keelward_logistics",
      "home_location_id": "loc_pressure_gate"
    },
    {
      "id": "chr_nia_okafor",
      "name": "Nia Okafor",
      "role": "supporting",
      "description": "A maintenance worker linked to the Shared Current, Nia was part of the crew that noticed its members finishing one another's sentences after working near the brood. She helped conceal the duplicate breeding logs in the Silt Archive's obsolete acoustic baffles because she wanted evidence beyond the contractors' competing reports. Compact and quick-moving, she keeps a grease pencil tucked behind one ear and writes down her own recollections to distinguish them from memories shared by others.",
      "motivation": "Protect the workers' ability to make choices for themselves, whether linked or not.",
      "goal": "Bring the hidden breeding-log copy into the open without allowing any corporation to seize it as exclusive property.",
      "flaw": "She assumes that secrecy preserves her independence, even when withholding information leaves others unable to consent.",
      "internal_conflict": "Shared memories make her feel less alone but also leave her uncertain which thoughts she should treat as private.",
      "external_conflict": "Pelagic, Meridian, and Keelward each have reasons to retrieve or destroy the logs, while the gate choice could strand workers or expose the colony.",
      "arc": "Nia begins hiding the Baffle Copy and keeping the linked workers' knowledge close, believing secrecy is their only leverage. When Tamsin asks the Shared Current to help judge the Pressure Gate choice, Nia must decide whether to reveal the logs and risk corporate seizure in order to let workers weigh the evidence themselves. She ends willing to share information with safeguards instead of using secrecy as a substitute for consent.",
      "personality_traits": [
        "resourceful",
        "wary",
        "empathetic",
        "independent"
      ],
      "abilities": [
        {
          "name": "Maintenance access",
          "description": "Knows service routes and concealed spaces in the colony, including the obsolete acoustic baffles in the Silt Archive.",
          "category": "technological"
        },
        {
          "name": "Shared perception",
          "description": "Can access memories and immediate perceptions shared by exposed workers, without being able to command them or guarantee agreement.",
          "category": "other"
        }
      ],
      "faction_id": "fac_shared_current",
      "home_location_id": "loc_silt_archive"
    },
    {
      "id": "chr_leviathan",
      "name": "The Largest Leviathan",
      "role": "supporting",
      "description": "The largest engineered animal in the Brood Vault, this leviathan was bred for a colony that valued its tissues and enzymes. It began arranging feeding lights into patterns that echoed fragments of a handler's memories; after workers were exposed to its recurring low-frequency biological signals, their perceptions and recollections began to overlap. No one can establish that the animal shares the workers' intentions, and its signals do not make the linked people a single obedient mind. Its vast silhouette moves through nutrient-rich water, marked by pale scars from enclosure hardware.",
      "motivation": "Continue its own existence and respond to the patterns and signals around it, though human motives cannot be confidently assigned to it.",
      "goal": "Remain alive and communicate through the biological signals and light patterns available to it.",
      "flaw": "Its contagious signals spread shared perceptions without providing a reliable way to establish each exposed worker's consent.",
      "internal_conflict": "Its emerging communication is entangled with the very exposure that blurs the boundary between its perceptions and the workers'.",
      "external_conflict": "Pelagic wants to capture it intact, Meridian wants to harvest it, and Keelward's sealed gate and station lockdown constrain every possible outcome.",
      "arc": "The leviathan begins communicating through repeated patterns that humans interpret as fragments of memory, while its signals continue to link nearby workers without clear consent. When Ilya discloses the anomaly report and the workers debate whether to approach or isolate it, the animal's pattern is met with a response rather than an extraction attempt. It ends still contained by the colony's choices, but recognized as a communicating being rather than merely a production asset.",
      "personality_traits": [
        "responsive",
        "unreadable",
        "persistent"
      ],
      "abilities": [
        {
          "name": "Low-frequency signaling",
          "description": "Produces recurring biological signals that can spread shared memories and immediate perceptions among workers exposed nearby.",
          "category": "other"
        },
        {
          "name": "Patterned light response",
          "description": "Arranges feeding-light patterns that workers recognize as echoes of remembered experiences.",
          "category": "other"
        }
      ],
      "home_location_id": "loc_brood_vault"
    }
  ],

    {

      "relationship_type": "uneasy ally",
      "description": "Nia Okafor can help Tamsin Reed understand the workers' shared perceptions, but distrusts Tamsin's control of the Pressure Gate and the information behind its lockdown."

      "source_character_id": "chr_leviathan",
      "target_character_id": "chr_ilya_voss",
      "relationship_type": "uneasy bond",
      "description": "The leviathan's patterns drew Ilya Voss into recognizing its signals, but her role in the breeding program makes its communication inseparable from the danger of corporate custody."
    },
    {
      "id": "rel_marek_tamsin",
      "source_character_id": "chr_marek_sato",
      "target_character_id": "chr_tamsin_reed",
      "relationship_type": "rival",
      "description": "Marek Sato wants the Enzyme Works to keep operating, while Tamsin Reed's sealed Pressure Gate and evacuation priorities can halt the production chain he is responsible for."
    }
  ]
